name: console-layout
purpose: The console chrome, composed once in the app: `AppLayout` with the navigation rail (`Sidebar` + `Menu`, the brand on top and the account at the foot), the global header (breadcrumbs, `SearchTrigger`, the app's own actions and the account avatar) and the `Command` search palette wired to the trigger and to ⌘K / Ctrl K. The navigation is data (`navigation`, each row with an `href` that is followed with the app's router when it is an in-app path), the active row follows the current route, and the page body is the default slot inside the layout's `<main>`. A page opens the palette with `useConsoleLayout().openSearch()`, sets its own trail with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs`, and fills a fixed-height main with `data-layout-fill` on its root. Platform blocks are only page bodies rendered through this slot; they never carry the chrome themselves.
useWhen: Every signed-in console page: put one `ConsoleLayout` in the app's root (around `RouterView`) and render each page block as its default slot.

A product area that needs the console navigation, breadcrumbs, the ⌘K palette and the account menu without hand-composing `AppLayout`, `Sidebar`, `Menu`, `GlobalHeader`, `SearchTrigger` and `Command`.
avoidWhen: A focused flow with no navigation rail (a creation wizard, sign-in) → render the page on its own or with the flow's own header.
When the page needs the split panel → compose `AppLayout` directly; `ConsoleLayout` covers the navigation, header, notifications, tools and content regions.
related: AppLayout` — the frame this layout fills; it owns the compact drawers and the scrolling content region.
Sidebar`, `Menu` — the rail and the data-driven navigation tree (`navigation` is mapped onto `Menu` groups).
SearchTrigger`, `Command` — the header search and the palette it opens; the palette lists every navigation page.
Breadcrumb` — the header trail on wide layouts (`breadcrumbs`).
shells/console` — the block that shows this layout with sample console navigation.
bestPractices: Compose the layout once, in the app's root, around `RouterView`; each route renders only its page body. Never copy the chrome into a page.

Give every navigation row an `id` and an `href`: an in-app path (`/workloads`) is followed with the app's router when one is installed (a named route becomes a path through `router.resolve(...).href`), an external URL loads normally, and a row with no `href` is left to your `navigate` handler. Never `to`, `path` or `route` on a row (lint `webkit/menu-node-href`). Leave `activeId` empty so the active row follows the route; set it only for a page whose route matches no row.
Pass a static trail through `breadcrumbs` (derive it from the route meta); leave it empty on first-level pages.

A page that owns its trail (a loaded name, a control crumb) renders `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs`: `items` are the crumbs, the default slot the trailing controls (a `Select` with `kind="transparent"`, `size="small"`, an `aria-label`, no `w-full`). It replaces the layout's trail while the page is mounted and renders nothing in place.
Put the app's own header actions (`Create`, `Agent`) in the `actions` slot and render them icon-only while `compact`.
Put the account menu groups (`DropdownMenu.Group`) in the `account-menu` slot; the layout renders the avatar and the trigger.
Put an account switcher in `header-start`, page-level flash messages in `notifications`, and help or the notifications list in `tools` (toggled from a bell in `actions` with `toggleTools`).
A page's control crumb is its `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs`, never `App.vue`'s `breadcrumbs` slot.

A workspace page (editor, pinned panes) puts `data-layout-fill` on its root: the `<main>` becomes a fixed-height, non-scrolling region the root fills. Never size a body with `100dvh` or `calc(100dvh - var(--layout-header-height))` (lint `webkit/no-viewport-height-calc`, also run by the authoring ratchet over blocks and examples).

Bind `v-model:navigation-expanded` when the rail's state must survive a reload or be driven from elsewhere (a `Collapse sidebar` / `Expand sidebar` command in the `search` slot); persist it in the app. The rail's own collapse control and the edge affordance keep working either way.

Open the palette from inside a page with `useConsoleLayout().openSearch()` (imported from `@aziontech/webkit/use-console-layout`); never mount a second `Command`. `useConsoleLayout()` throws outside a `ConsoleLayout`, so a misplaced call fails loudly.

A page body that also renders on its own (a block preview, a docs example, a test) calls `useConsoleLayout({ optional: true })`, which returns `null` outside a layout, and guards the call (`layout?.openSearch()`). Never wrap `useConsoleLayout()` in `try` / `catch`.

The page entrance (`animate-page-enter`) plays on every route path change: the `<main>` is keyed on the path, so the page body remounts when the path changes and is kept when only the query or the hash changes. Keep state that must survive a path change (a list filter, a draft) in the route query or in the app's store, not in the page body; a `KeepAlive` belongs inside a page body (tabbed views), not around `RouterView`.

The page body renders no `<main>` of its own and no `AppLayout`: the layout owns the landmark. Frame the body with `layout-boundary` + `layout-column` for list and form pages, or flush (`PageTabs` first) for detail pages.

props.name: navigation
props.doc: The navigation tree: groups of rows, each `{ id, label, icon?, href?, tagValue?, disabled?, kind?, children?, groups? }`; an in-app `href` is followed with the app's router.

props.name: activeId
props.doc: Id of the current row. Empty matches the current route against each row's `href`.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.doc: The trail shown in the header on wide layouts; each is `{ label, href? }` and the last one is the current page.

props.name: account
props.doc: The signed-in account, `{ name, email?, src? }`, shown at the foot of the rail and as the header avatar; nothing is rendered when absent.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Main navigation`).

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.doc: Placeholder of the palette's input. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Search pages and commands`).

props.name: toolsLabel
props.doc: Title of the tools region (help, notifications). Empty uses `AppLayout`'s catalog (`Help`).

events.name: navigate
events.notes: Fired when a navigation row or a palette page is chosen; the layout then follows its `href` (an in-app path with the app's router). A row without `href` is left to this handler. Event first.

events.name: search-select
events.notes: Fired when a palette item from the `search` slot is chosen; `value` is that item's value. Event first.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The page body, rendered inside the layout's `<main>`; a body whose root carries `data-layout-fill` fills a fixed-height, non-scrolling main.

slots.name: actions
slots.notes: The app's header actions, between the search trigger and the avatar; render them icon-only while `compact`; `toggleTools` opens and closes the tools region (a notifications bell).

slots.name: header-start
slots.notes: Content at the start of the header, before the breadcrumbs (an account or organization switcher).

slots.name: breadcrumbs
slots.notes: An app-wide composed trail that replaces the one built from `breadcrumbs`; a page's `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs` replaces both; hidden while compact.

slots.name: notifications
slots.notes: Flash messages (`Alert`) above the page, kept in view while the page scrolls.

slots.name: tools
slots.notes: The tools region's body (a `HelpPanel` or the notifications list), opened with `v-model:tools-open`.

slots.name: search
slots.notes: Extra `Command.Group`s (recent resources, commands) listed before the navigation pages in the palette.

slots.name: account-menu
slots.notes: DropdownMenu.Group`s of the account menu, opened from the account row in the rail and from the header avatar.
